description: Auto-checked  travel insurance without explicit consent.
explanation: Optional protection or service insurance was opted-in automatically by default.
The baseline advertised price does not reflect the unavoidable processing charges added on step 2.
Unchecking the option triggers a cautionary confirmation dialog.
recommendation: Audit every pre-ticked checkbox before authorizing payment and verify the final line item totals.

description: Subscription takes 1 click to join, but requires 6-step questionnaire, phone call during business hours, and emotional guilt buttons to cancel.
explanation: The 'Cancel Subscription' link is buried in fine print inside Settings > Billing > Advanced Preferences.
The confirmation button reads 'No thanks, I prefer being out of shape and losing my progress', while the cancel link is low-contrast gray text.
Final screen demands calling a toll phone line between 9am-12pm EST instead of providing automated online cancellation.
recommendation: Use a virtual credit card or request a merchant block via your bank if online cancellation is deliberately obstructed.

description: High-pressure flashing countdown timer ('05:00 remaining before tickets are released!') resets back to 05:00 on page reload.
explanation: The timer is implemented purely client-side via JavaScript `setInterval` without server-side cart reservation.
Simulated notification popups claim 'Sarah from Chicago just purchased 4 tickets' every 12 seconds using random name arrays.
Creates artificial panic to prevent price comparison across ticket marketplaces.
recommendation: Don't rush checkout decisions under flashing timers; refresh or check alternate vendor tabs to verify actual availability.

description: Advertised room rate was $119/night, but a mandatory $45 'Resort Experience Fee' and $18 'City Cleaning Levy' were injected on final step.
explanation: Initial search listings prominently show '$119 / night' with 'Taxes Included' misleading text.
Mandatory resort fee is only unveiled on page 4 after collecting credit card details.
Total price jumped from $238 to $364 for a 2-night stay with zero optional perks.
recommendation: File a consumer protection complaint under drip pricing transparency regulations and verify all-in totals before authorizing cards.

description: Adding a gaming laptop automatically placed a 2-year accidental damage insurance policy ($89.99) into the cart without asking.
explanation: The product page had no checkbox for the warranty, yet the checkout cart injected it as a bundled item.
The 'Remove' button for the warranty is styled as faint light gray text without standard trash icon.
Checkout button text says 'Proceed to 1-Click Pay' to discourage inspecting line items.
recommendation: Inspect every line item in your cart before pressing payment authorization, especially on electronics retailers.

description: Pre-selected $34 travel insurance checkbox and auto-added priority boarding without user consent.
explanation: The 'Comprehensive Flight Guard ($34.99)' checkbox is enabled by default in the passenger add-on screen.
The opt-out requires scrolling past three marketing paragraphs and unchecking a muted gray box.
The total price changes at the final payment step without a clear line-item difference callout.
recommendation: Always uncheck optional add-on checkboxes before proceeding to payment, and compare the subtotal on step 1 with the final charge.
